title: Warmer Day Wait
statement:
For every day in a temperature log, count how many days you must wait until a strictly warmer day arrives.

Contract
- `temperatures` is non-null and may be empty; values may be any `int`, including negative ones.
- The result has the same length as `temperatures`. Entry `i` is the smallest `d > 0` with `temperatures[i + d] > temperatures[i]`.
- If no later day is strictly warmer, entry `i` is `0`. An equal temperature is not warmer.
- Do not mutate `temperatures`.

Examples
- `daysUntilWarmer(new int[]{68, 70, 65, 66, 72, 60})` returns `[1, 3, 1, 1, 0, 0]`.
- `daysUntilWarmer(new int[]{50, 50, 50})` returns `[0, 0, 0]`.
- `daysUntilWarmer(new int[]{60, 61, 62, 63})` returns `[1, 1, 1, 0]`.
hints: Looking forward from every day with a nested loop works but repeats a lot of work when many days are cold.
Walk the days once while keeping the days still waiting for a warmer one. A warmer reading settles every waiting day that is colder than it.

Keep the waiting days on a stack of indices whose temperatures never increase from bottom to top; pop while the new day is warmer and record the gap. Intended complexity: O(n) time because each index is pushed and popped once, and O(n) space for the result and the stack, where n is the number of days.
inputSyntax: Input: the daily temperatures, for example: [68, 70, 65, 66, 72, 60]
